findings.text: follow-on: _declared_group_members is a verbatim duplicate of reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:1291 -- same name, same signature, same body: i.e. `tuple(budget_group.declared_groups(config).get(str(group), ()))` -- so the name now means two things in one package and the two copies can drift independently. budget.py already imports budget_group at line 62, so this could import the sibling or resolve declared_groups at each site rather than growing a second private wrapper.

follow-on: _published_point selects the first payload entry carrying a numeric utilisation, and budget_lift.published_readings orders those entries by figure order, which is five_hour before seven_day (reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:57 PERIODS = window_reading.PERIODS = ("five_hour", "seven_day")). The recorded series _group_points builds applies no period filter either, so on a lane that publishes both windows the point added is the five-hour window's utilisation and reset while the recorded readings are whatever window the live pointer carried; the resulting window_rate_pct_per_hour and window_even_share_pct then mix two windows. The new test publishes only seven_day, so no case exercises the multi-window document and I could not settle whether a metered lane's recorded utilisation_pct and its published five_hour figure are ever the same window. Flagging as a reading, not a proven production wrong: worth a case that publishes both windows before the figure is trusted on a two-window lane.

follow-on: the node's done-when requires `ruff check and ruff format --check add no finding on the staged paths, judged against the base blobs, with the log in the run directory`, and no ruff log exists in the run directory (it holds only base-arm.log, head-arm.log, negative-control.log). I re-ran the check independently: ruff check adds no finding on the staged paths at head against the base blobs (budget.py 1 ISC004 at 1670 vs base 1 at 1314, _flight_schema.py 35 vs 35, all pre-existing), and ruff format --check reports the same single pre-existing file at both revisions, so the claim is true but the artefact the done-when names is absent and the fragment's ruff sentence currently rests on an unrecorded claim. Also, baseline_suite/after_suite carry the angle-bracket placeholder commands `<50-file gate minus the new test file>`/`<the same 50-file gate>` and the manifest tests: line is a description rather than the literal command, so the gate receipt is not replayable from the record even though the logs' own `# command:` headers carry the literal invocation.
